title: Fppf local conjugacy of geometrically maximal tori
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [pqf-def-affine-morphism] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A group scheme over $S$ is a group object in schemes over $S$; finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $T_0,T_1\hookrightarrow G$ be closed subgroup schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], both relative $S$-tori [def-sfb-relative-torus]. Suppose that for every geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, each $(T_a)_{\bar s}$ is maximal under inclusion among torus subgroups of $G_{\bar s}$, where a torus over $\Omega$ is a group scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,\Omega}^d$ for some $d\geq0$. Then there is an fppf covering $\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] and elements $g_i\in G(S_i)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(S_i,G)$ such that $g_i(T_0)_{S_i}g_i^{-1}=(T_1)_{S_i}$ as closed subgroup schemes of $G_{S_i}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. This equality is an equality of subgroup functors on all $S_i$-schemes, including nonreduced test schemes. No reductivity, connectedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed, and ranks may vary with the base.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.2.6, printed pp.94-95: after the paragraph ending "Now we will just use that G to S is a smooth S-affine group", the two-maximal-tori argument uses direct limits (Lemma 3.2.5), completion and approximation, and Corollary B.3.5. This is only the conjugacy input, not the parameter-scheme theorem. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative group-scheme structural result.

proof.text: It suffices to construct the required covering after an fppf covering of the base: compose the local coverings, using the covering transitivity axiom. First cover S by affine opens. On each such open, the definition of a relative torus supplies splitting fppf coverings for T_0 and T_1; pull one back along the other and compose. Refine by the affine-refinement lemma. Thus we may work over a nonempty affine S=Spec A on which T_a is identified with the split torus of rank r_a, for a=0,1. The empty affine needs no covering members. Base change preserves smoothness of G. Geometric maximality is inherited because every algebraically closed geometric point of any new base is also such a point of the original base.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2, proof, printed pp.56-57: local splitting and reduction to affine bases; covering transitivity is Stacks Tag 00VH, affine refinement Tag 021L.

proof.text: Write G=Spec C. The affine smoothness equivalence identifies A to C as a smooth ring map. The smooth-algebra model theorem gives a finitely generated integer subring A_0 of A and a smooth affine finite-presentation scheme G_0=Spec C_0 whose base change is G. Enlarge A_0 through the directed set of finitely generated subrings of A when necessary, replacing G_0 by base change; smoothness persists. This directed system has limit Spec A by Noetherian approximation. Every stage is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Z lemma, and every scheme used as a finite product of G_0 and split tori is affine, hence qcqs.

source.place: Tag 00TP, lemma-finite-presentation-fs-Noetherian; Limits Tag 01YW and Properties Tag 01OU. Conrad Proposition 2.1.2, first reduction, printed pp.56-57.

proof.text: Descend the multiplication, identity and inverse of G, and both maps from the standard split tori into G, by the arrow clause of finite-presentation spreading out. Use the standard split tori and the finite products of G_0 as the chosen object models. The associativity, unit, inverse and subgroup-homomorphism diagrams are finitely many equalities of maps between those finite-presentation models. The equality clause therefore makes all diagrams hold at a common later stage. The two descended torus maps are locally of finite type (their affine source algebras have finite generating sets already over the base); the closed-immersion descent lemma makes both maps closed immersions after a further enlargement. We now have a smooth affine finite-type group G_0 over a nonzero Noetherian ring A_0, with closed split torus subgroups T_{0,0},T_{1,0}, whose entire diagram pulls back to the prescribed one. No geometric maximality assertion at this stage is needed.

source.place: Tags 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (2),(3), and 01ZP, lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation; the finite group-diagram argument is the first paragraph of Conrad Proposition 2.1.2.

proof.text: Apply the existing multiplicative-type transporter theorem to G_0 and the two split tori. It gives a closed finite-presentation smooth A_0-scheme Z_0 representing gT_{0,0}g^{-1} contained in T_{1,0}. Pull back along Spec A to Spec A_0. Its arbitrary-base-change assertion says exactly that Z=Z_0 times_{A_0} A represents g(T_0)_Vg^{-1} contained in (T_1)_V, as subgroup functors on every V-scheme. In particular there is a universal g in G(Z) and a unique induced group homomorphism q:(T_0)_Z to (T_1)_Z, with j_1 q=Int(g)j_0. The group diagrams follow since j_1 is monic. Smoothness of Z over S follows from smooth base change.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2, printed pp.56-60, including functorial base change. Only containment is asserted here.

proof.text: For each geometric point s:Spec Omega to S, consider G_s. Its identity component G_s^0 is an open and closed connected subgroup of finite type. It is affine by the closed-immersion affine criterion and smooth by restriction of the smooth morphism G_s to its open component. Each split torus (T_a)_s is connected: its Laurent coordinate ring over Omega is a domain (including rank zero), so its spectrum is irreducible. Its image contains the identity and therefore lies in the identity component. Factor through that open component by the open-factorization lemma; the torus remains a closed subgroup there. A larger torus in G_s^0 would be a larger torus in G_s, so both tori are maximal in G_s^0. The classical Borel/maximal-torus conjugacy theorem, applied to this smooth connected affine Omega-group, supplies h in G_s^0(Omega) with h(T_0)_s h^{-1}=(T_1)_s as subgroup schemes. Consequently h defines an Omega-point of Z above s. Every point of S admits an algebraically closed residue-field extension, so Z to S is surjective.

source.place: Corollary 2.1.5, printed pp.60-61, and Theorem 3.2.6, conjugacy paragraph, printed p.95; classical conjugacy: Milne Theorem 17.10, printed pp.354-355; identity subgroup: Stacks Tag 0B7R.

proof.text: The universal containment is an equality on Z, not just on its geometric points. Indeed, at every algebraically closed geometric point z of Z, q_z identifies the conjugate of the maximal torus (T_0)_z with a torus subgroup of (T_1)_z. Maximality in G_z makes this inclusion an equality. Apply the split-torus matrix-sheaf theorem to q over Z. Locally on Z it is given by a constant integer matrix M. If that open is nonempty, choose a geometric point of it. Since q_z is an isomorphism, the matrix correspondence and its composition law give an integer inverse of M there: r_0=r_1 and M is unimodular. The same constant inverse defines an inverse homomorphism throughout that open. These local inverses agree because they are inverses of q, so q is an isomorphism. Thus j_1 q=Int(g)j_0 gives g(T_0)_Zg^{-1}=(T_1)_Z as subgroup functors on every Z-scheme, with no reducedness assumption.

source.place: Corollary 2.1.5, final sentence of proof, printed p.61: equality checked after splitting via characters; Proposition B.1.1, printed pp.280-281. This is the explicit matrix argument, not a fibrewise equality criterion for arbitrary closed subschemes.

proof.text: The smooth surjection Z to S is flat and locally of finite presentation by the smooth-flat lemma. By the definition of the fppf site, its singleton is an fppf covering. Its universal element g gives the required conjugation by step 6. For the original base, compose these coverings with the affine splitting coverings of step 1, using site transitivity. Empty pieces contribute no members. Ranks are fixed only on each splitting member; the construction requires no global rank, connectedness of G, reductivity or Noetherian condition on S.

Its 7 steps are a correct assembly in the spirit of Conrad 2.1.2/2.1.5 and match the cited statements. Step 1: fppf splitting covers (def-sfb-relative-torus), pulled back with lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change, composed by site transitivity and made affine with lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement. Step 2: smooth finite-type model over a finitely generated subring A_0 and the Nagata limit. Step 3: thm-pd-spreading-out clauses (2) and (3) descend the group structure and the torus maps, and 01ZP closed-immersion descent applies because the maps are lft and everything is affine and qcqs; maximality is never descended. Step 4: the transporter node's hypotheses (Noetherian nonzero A_0, smooth affine finite-type G_0, split tori of multiplicative type) hold, and its base-change clause carries the transporter to Spec A. Step 5: G_s^0 is affine, smooth and connected; the tori factor through it and stay maximal; Borel/Milne 17.10 conjugacy gives surjectivity of Z→S. Step 6: the matrix-sheaf node holds over any base, so the integer inverse at a geometric point inverts q on the whole open; marking it elementary is fine. Step 7: smooth gives flat and lfp, so {Z→S} is an fppf cover. Edge cases checked: empty S, rank 0, disconnected G, nonreduced base, non-Noetherian A. No cycle (closure traversed) and no duplicate (searched 'maximal tor'; lem-sfb-isogeny-torus-conjugacy is a different statement). Batch-5 check: lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change, lem-trf-finite-type-component-open-qc and lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent are generic scheme and site facts, not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so all four flagged citations are accepted. The tool_uses are accepted as generic tools. Conrad is not archived locally (WANTED); the proof depends only on DAG statements.
